standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic safe execution task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: With permission granted, materials ready, and communication complete, the learner carries out the project itself on a scheduled day, working through the ordered steps from the planning lesson while a trusted adult supervises directly for any step involving tools, physical strain, heat, chemicals, or unfamiliar surroundings.
safetyNotes: Any step of the project that involves tools, lifting, heat, cleaning products, or being outdoors away from your household's immediate space is done by or directly alongside a trusted adult.
Stay within the exact scope that was agreed to in the permission conversation — do not add new tasks, people, or locations once the project is underway.
Stop and ask your trusted adult for help immediately if anything about the project feels unsafe, goes differently than planned, or you are unsure what to do next.

simulationAlternative.description: If the project cannot be carried out for real this week, the learner instead completes a detailed walk-through of the execution plan: narrating each ordered step out loud or in writing, in the exact order from the planning lesson, including exactly what the trusted adult would be doing at each step, without carrying out the project for real yet.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l05-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l05-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l05-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l05-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain the moment during execution when your trusted adult's supervision mattered most, and what might have gone wrong without it.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u06-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Plan adherence and safety: Steps are completed in the planned order, and every physically risky step is documented as directly supervised by a trusted adult. | Real-time problem handling: A specific step that went differently than planned is described along with how the learner and trusted adult handled it. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner write a short list of what they would change about the execution plan itself, separate from the outcome, if they were to do this same project again.

resources.title: safe execution worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: With permission granted, materials ready, and communication complete, the learner carries out the project itself on a scheduled day, working through the ordered steps from the planning lesson while a trusted adult supervises directly for any step involving tools, physical strain, heat, chemicals, or unfamiliar surroundings.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact safe execution decision or action.
Model move 2: Before starting, review your ordered step list and confirm your trusted adult knows the plan and is available to supervise.

Model move 3: Work through your ordered steps one at a time with your trusted adult directly supervising any step involving tools, heat, chemicals, lifting, or being outdoors away from home, checking off each step as you finish it.

Model check: Plan adherence and safety: Steps are completed in the planned order, and every physically risky step is documented as directly supervised by a trusted adult. | Real-time problem handling: A specific step that went differently than planned is described along with how the learner and trusted adult handled it.

resources.title: safe execution action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for safe execution.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: safe execution coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: With permission granted, materials ready, and communication complete, the learner carries out the project itself on a scheduled day, working through the ordered steps from the planning lesson while a trusted adult supervises directly for any step involving tools, physical strain, heat, chemicals, or unfamiliar surroundings.
Coach direction: Before starting, review your ordered step list and confirm your trusted adult knows the plan and is available to supervise.
Learner prompt: I reviewed my full ordered step list with a trusted adult immediately before starting.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: safe execution complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Work through your ordered steps one at a time with your trusted adult directly supervising any step involving tools, heat, chemicals, lifting, or being outdoors away from home, checking off each step as you finish it.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I completed each step in the order from my plan, checking it off as I finished.
Response 2 (t2-p2): A trusted adult was directly present or supervising for every step that involved physical risk.

Equal-access rule: If the project cannot be carried out for real this week, the learner instead completes a detailed walk-through of the execution plan: narrating each ordered step out loud or in writing, in the exact order from the planning lesson, including exactly what the trusted adult would be doing at each step, without carrying out the project for real yet.

resources.title: safe execution minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain the moment during execution when your trusted adult's supervision mattered most, and what might have gone wrong without it.

Success checks: Plan adherence and safety: Steps are completed in the planned order, and every physically risky step is documented as directly supervised by a trusted adult. | Real-time problem handling: A specific step that went differently than planned is described along with how the learner and trusted adult handled it.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: safe execution supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l05-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g7-u06-l05-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional safe execution condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Plan adherence and safety: Steps are completed in the planned order, and every physically risky step is documented as directly supervised by a trusted adult. | Real-time problem handling: A specific step that went differently than planned is described along with how the learner and trusted adult handled it..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l05-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

realRoute.title: safe execution — permitted real-life route
realRoute.permissionRule: Do not begin the physical action until a household-authorized guardian gives permission and is available for the supervision or review named in this lesson.
steps: Confirm the setting, materials, and stop condition before acting.

Work through your ordered steps one at a time with your trusted adult directly supervising any step involving tools, heat, chemicals, lifting, or being outdoors away from home, checking off each step as you finish it.
Complete the response prompts on the delivered independent card without recording private identifying details.
Check the result against the delivered evidence record and correct any missed step.
realRoute.completionCondition: The learner submits the minimal process record; only the household-authorized guardian attests that the named physical action occurred.

simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u06-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Plan adherence and safety: Steps are completed in the planned order, and every physically risky step is documented as directly supervised by a trusted adult. | Real-time problem handling: A specific step that went differently than planned is described along with how the learner and trusted adult handled it.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
